api.intro: Lets other programs use the agent runtimes installed on this computer through the standard OpenAI API: point any OpenAI SDK or tool at the base URL with one of this profile's API keys.

classHint.chatOnly: No tools: monomind's tool gate leaves the runtime nothing to use, so it answers in text.
classHint.sandboxed: Writes are confined to the turn's folder; it can still read files and use the network.
classHint.unconfined: Its native tools run as your user account.
classHint.any: Serves every class, unconfined runtimes included.

status.exposureLoopbackHint: Listens on loopback only, so other computers can't connect to it directly. A reverse proxy, tunnel or port forward on this computer can still expose it.
status.exposureNetworkHint: Other computers can reach it, over TLS.
status.noteNoneDaemon: The daemon is running but serves no /v1: it serves no HTTP API (see --api and --api-addr) and has no dedicated listener (--v1-addr).
status.noteDown: Nothing answers at {{addr}}. Start the daemon (monoagentcli daemon) or monoagentcli httpapi.
status.noteDownDaemon: Nothing answers at {{addr}}, although the daemon is running. It may still be starting, or it does not serve the API there (see --api, --api-addr and --v1-addr, and the daemon's log).
status.noteBadAddr: The address {{addr}} is not a host name or IP address with a port, so no base URL is shown for it.
status.noteNoV1Daemon: The daemon does not serve /v1 on {{addr}}: another process may own the API's working folders (see the daemon's log).
status.noteNoV1Offloopback: {{addr}} is not loopback, so /v1 is not served there. Give it its own listener with --v1-addr (TLS only).
status.noteStale: {{addr}} answers /health but not /v1: a server that predates the API may still be running. Restart it.
status.noteTls: TLS only. Clients must trust the server's certificate: a self-signed one unless MONOAGENT_API_TLS_CERT and MONOAGENT_API_TLS_KEY are set.
status.noteWildcard: The server listens on every interface. From another computer, use this computer's address instead of localhost.
status.noteAssumed: Assumed from this app's environment: a server started with --confinement, --context-confinement or --auto-confinement may differ.

keys.title: API keys
keys.hint: A key belongs to this profile: requests made with it run as this profile. Only its hash is kept, so a key is shown once, when you create it.
keys.empty: No API keys yet. Create one to let a program use the API.
keys.contextHint: Context adds excerpts of this profile's documents and captures to every request made with the key. Such a key is served only by models up to {{class}} (--context-confinement).
keys.contextHintMany: Context adds excerpts of this profile's documents and captures to every request made with the key. Such a key is served only by models up to the class each listener allows (--context-confinement, see above).
keys.revokeBody: Programs that use "{{name}}" stop working at their next request. This can't be undone.

create.title: Create an API key
create.name: Name
create.nameHint: 1 to 64 characters: letters, digits, space, . _ -, starting with a letter or digit.
create.context: Add this profile's knowledge to requests (context)
create.contextHint: Excerpts of this profile's documents and captures go into each prompt, so they reach the model's provider. A key with context is served only by chat-only models unless the server raises --context-confinement.
create.warning: Copy it now. This is the only time the key is shown: only its hash is kept.
create.copyFailed: Couldn't copy: select the key and copy it by hand.
create.usage: Use it as the API key of an OpenAI client, with the base URL of this section.
create.noKey: monoagentcli did not return the key. Revoke this key and create another.

models.title: Models
models.policyDaemon: Policy of the listener at {{addr}}, as the running daemon reports it.
models.policyAssumed: Policy of the listener at {{addr}}, assumed from this app's environment.
models.policyDefault: No listener serves /v1 right now: this is what this app's own settings would serve on a loopback listener.
models.policyUnknown: Couldn't read which listeners serve /v1, so this is what this app's own settings would serve on a loopback listener, not necessarily what the running server serves.
models.policyMany: {{count}} listeners serve /v1, each with its own policy: this table is the one for {{addr}}.
models.capImageHint: Image generation: it can answer POST /v1/images/generations.
models.capToolsHint: Tool calling (function calling): a request can declare tools and get a tool call back for the client to run.
models.empty: No models found. Install an agent runtime on the AI agents page.
models.autoLabel: Jev picks the model for each request
models.autoOn_one: On. Only {{count}} model is allowed here (up to {{class}}), so auto uses it without asking Jev.
models.autoOn_other: On. Jev picks among the {{count}} models it may use here (up to {{class}}).
models.autoOnPlain: On. Jev picks among the models it may use here.
models.autoHeldBack_one: {{count}} more model is served here but is above {{class}}, so auto may not pick it. Raise it with --auto-confinement (MONOAGENT_API_AUTO_CONFINEMENT) on the server.
models.autoHeldBack_other: {{count}} more models are served here but are above {{class}}, so auto may not pick them. Raise it with --auto-confinement (MONOAGENT_API_AUTO_CONFINEMENT) on the server.
models.autoKeyEnv: The Jev key is this app's TYPESAFE_API_KEY: a running server reads its own environment.
models.openJevHint: The Jev key and the api_auto feature are switched on there.

errors.nameTaken: An active key of this profile already has that name. Pick another name.
errors.nameInvalid: That name isn't allowed. Use 1 to 64 characters: letters, digits, space, . _ -, starting with a letter or digit, and not shaped like a key id (key_ and 12 characters).
errors.keyNotFound: That key no longer exists: it may have been revoked from the terminal or another window.

errors.maxConcurrent: The number of turns at once must be a whole number from {{min}} to {{max}}.
errors.turnTimeout: The turn timeout must be a duration of at least {{min}}, such as {{example}}.
errors.class: That isn't a class. Use chat-only, sandboxed or any.
errors.addr: The address must be host:port, such as 127.0.0.1:9443 or :9443.
errors.imageRuntimes: Give a comma-separated list of runtime ids, or none to switch image generation off.
errors.toolRuntimes: Give a comma-separated list of runtime ids, or none to switch tool calling off.
errors.empty: A value is needed here. To go back to the default, use “Use the default”.
errors.tlsPair: The certificate file and the key file are saved together: give both.
errors.tlsAbsolute: A TLS file needs an absolute path: the daemon starts in another folder, and ~ is not expanded.
errors.controlChars: A value can't contain control characters, such as a line break or a tab.
errors.widenedMeanwhile: Nothing was saved: the saved settings changed meanwhile, and this change now makes the server reach further. Try again to review it.
errors.notRegistered: The daemon isn't registered for auto-start, so nothing can restart it from here.

v1_addr.label: Dedicated /v1 listener
v1_addr.hint: Where /v1 listens besides the main HTTP API, as host:port, such as 0.0.0.0:9443. Beyond this computer it speaks TLS only.

tls.label: TLS certificate and key
tls.hint: Absolute paths of the PEM files for that listener, read when the server starts. Give both, or neither for a self-signed certificate.

confinement.label: Strongest class served
confinement.hint: chat-only, sandboxed or any: the strongest class of agent runtime the server serves.
confinement.empty: Default: any on loopback, chat-only beyond

context_confinement.label: Strongest class for keys with context
context_confinement.hint: A key created with context is served by runtimes up to this class, and never above the strongest class served.

auto_confinement.label: Strongest class auto may pick
auto_confinement.hint: The auto model picks among runtimes up to this class, and never above the strongest class served.

max_concurrent.label: Turns at once
max_concurrent.hint: How many requests run at the same time. Beyond that the server answers 429.

turn_timeout.label: Turn timeout
turn_timeout.hint: The longest one turn may run, such as 15m.

image_runtimes.label: Runtimes that make images
image_runtimes.hint: Comma-separated runtime ids whose models serve image generation, or none to switch it off.

tool_runtimes.label: Runtimes that serve tool calling
tool_runtimes.hint: Comma-separated runtime ids whose models serve tool calling, or none to switch it off.

stateHint.applied: The running daemon uses the saved value, or the default where none is saved.
stateHint.pending: Saved after the running daemon started: it uses it once it restarts.
stateHint.overridden: The daemon was started with its own flag or environment variable for this setting, so a saved value has no effect until that is removed.
stateHint.notRunning: No daemon is running. The server reads the saved value when it starts.
stateHint.unknown: The running daemon predates the settings report, so what it runs is unknown. Restart it to be sure.
stateHint.notServing: The daemon took this value, but the dedicated /v1 listener it describes is not up. The daemon's log says why, for example a certificate file that cannot be read or a port already in use. Correct the setting, or the file or port it names, then restart the daemon.

kind.confinement: A stronger class of runtime is served
kind.context_confinement: Keys with context may use more
kind.saved_settings: What the saved settings limited is unknown

widening.title: This change makes the server reach further
widening.introSave: Saving it lets the server reach further than it does now:
widening.introUnset: Going back to the default lets the server reach further than it does now:
widening.note: It applies the next time the daemon starts.
widening.confirmUnset: Use the default and allow this
widening.introReset: Resetting removes the saved settings, which can't be read. Every setting goes back to its environment variable or its default, which may let the server reach further than it does now:

config.title: Server settings
config.hint: What the server reads when it starts. A daemon reads the saved settings the next time it starts, unless a flag or an environment variable of its own sets them.
config.overriddenFlag: The daemon was started with {{name}}, so a saved value has no effect until that flag is removed.
config.overriddenEnv: The daemon's environment sets {{name}}, so a saved value has no effect until that variable is removed.
config.problemHint: Remove the saved value with “Use the default”, or save a valid one.

banner.restartBody: The running daemon started before these were saved, so it still runs the old values: {{keys}}. It reads the saved settings when it restarts.
banner.olderBody: The running daemon predates the settings report, so what it runs is unknown. Restart it to be sure it reads the saved settings.
banner.idleBody: No daemon is running: the server reads these settings when it starts.
banner.notServingBody: The daemon runs, but its dedicated listener is not up: {{keys}}. Its log says why, for example a certificate file that cannot be read or a port already in use. Correct the setting, or the file or port it names, then restart the daemon.

note.unchanged: Nothing changed: it is already saved like this.
note.also: This also makes the server reach further, in ways the dialog did not list:

restart.title: Restart the daemon?
restart.body: Restarting stops the daemon and starts it again. It interrupts whatever the daemon is running: workflows and org runs.
restart.after: Then this page checks that the daemon is back and runs what is saved.
restart.checking: Waiting for the daemon to report back…
restart.back: The daemon is back and runs the saved settings.
restart.backListenerDown: The daemon is back, but its dedicated listener is not up. Its log says why.
restart.late: The daemon hasn't reported back yet. Refresh to check again.
restart.notDone: The service manager did not restart the daemon.
restart.noAutostart: The daemon isn't registered for auto-start, so this page can't restart it. Stop it, then start it again:
restart.install: To let this page restart it next time, register it first:
restart.byHand: If a daemon was also started by hand, stop it first: the service's daemon would find that one running and exit.

reset.done: The saved settings were reset. Every setting is back to its environment variable or its default.

scope.globalLine: Applies to this whole machine, every profile.
scope.profileLine: Applies only to the profile {{name}}. Other profiles keep their own.
scope.profileLineNoName: Applies only to the active profile. Other profiles keep their own.

jev.consent: Turning a feature on is a choice for this profile only: it lets this profile send data to TypeSafe. Other profiles stay off until they turn it on themselves.
jev.adoptHint: This key is still only in this profile's vault. To share it with every profile, run:

profile.deleteHint: Deleting a profile removes its data. You will be asked three times.
profile.onlyProfile: This is your only profile. Create another one before deleting it.
profile.step1Detail: That includes its people and messages, workflows and their files, tasks, publications, vault items and documents, credentials and API keys, chats and orgs, and its vault key. It does NOT include its folder {{folder}} or its synced message attachments (in ~/.monoagent/attachments): those stay on disk.
profile.step2Total: This cannot be undone. {{count}} stored items will be deleted for good.
profile.step2Active: This is the profile you are using: the app will switch to another one.
profile.step2Backup: First, a copy of the whole database is saved in the backups folder next to it. It holds every profile, not only this one, is not encrypted, and is never deleted automatically (`monoagentcli profile backups purge` removes these copies). The profile's vault key is deleted, so the vault secrets in that copy cannot be decrypted. Running orgs of this profile are stopped first, and browsers bound to it are unbound.
profile.step2Ack: I understand this cannot be undone
profile.step3Intro: Final check. Type {{name}} to delete it.
profile.doneBackup: A copy of the database was saved to {{path}}. It holds every profile and is never deleted automatically.

auto.label: Re-check stale models automatically
auto.help: When on, the daemon re-checks stale models in the background while no chat, workflow or org is running (after {{quiet}} of quiet, never at startup): at most {{perDay}} runtime(s) a day, {{models}} model(s) each.
auto.money: Each re-check is a real model call and costs money.
auto.noDaemon: The daemon isn't running, so nothing runs until it starts.
auto.fromTable: ({{count}} priced from the built-in price table)
auto.confirmBody: The daemon will make real, paid model calls without asking: up to {{perDay}} runtime(s) a day, {{models}} model(s) each.

expired.title: Your sign-in has expired
expired.body: MonoAgent could not reach monoes.me for more than a day. Check your connection, then sign in again.

refused.title: monoes.me ended this sign-in
refused.body: This account can no longer use MonoAgent. If you think that is a mistake, contact monoes.me support. You can sign in with another account.

clock.title: This computer's clock looks wrong
clock.body: MonoAgent saw a time that does not fit monoes.me's clock. Set the date and time right, then sign in again.

keyUnknown.title: This version cannot verify your sign-in
keyUnknown.body: monoes.me signs logins with a newer key than this version of MonoAgent knows. Update MonoAgent, then sign in again.

unconfirmed.title: This computer stopped using its saved sign-in
unconfirmed.body: monoes.me may have received a refresh whose answer never arrived, so this computer stopped using its saved sign-in to protect your other installs. Sign in again on this computer.

invalid.title: Your sign-in could not be verified
invalid.body: The saved sign-in is damaged or was not issued for MonoAgent. Sign in again.

cliNotFound.title: MonoAgent cannot find its command-line tool
cliNotFound.body: MonoAgent needs monoagentcli to check your sign-in and cannot find it. Reinstall MonoAgent, or point MONOAGENTCLI_BIN at a current monoagentcli.

cliTooOld.title: MonoAgent's command-line tool is out of date
cliTooOld.body: The monoagentcli this app found does not support monoes.me accounts, or speaks a newer version than this app. Update MonoAgent to bring both up to date.

cliFailed.title: MonoAgent could not check your sign-in
cliFailed.body: monoagentcli did not give an answer. Try again, or update MonoAgent.

update.upToDate: MonoAgent is already up to date.

grace.keyringUnavailable: MonoAgent cannot open the key store to refresh your sign-in.
grace.unconfirmed: monoes.me may have received a refresh whose answer never arrived, so this computer can no longer renew its sign-in. It works until {{when}} ({{left}}); sign in again before then.
grace.keepsWorking: Your sign-in keeps working offline until {{when}} ({{left}}).

warn.text: A monoes.me sign-in will be required from {{date}}.

tasks.title: Tasks
tasks.readOnly: Read-only: this app was started by an agent, so only people change the board.
tasks.leaseEnded: The lease ended: another agent may take it over, or it can go back to Ready.

drawer.title: Title
drawer.readFirst: This card has notes. Read them before you approve it: in Ready, agents act on its whole text.
drawer.readFirstMove: This card has notes. Read them before it leaves Inbox: agents act on its whole text.

emptyBy.inbox: Highlight text in Chrome and choose MonoAgent, Add selection as task, or select text in any app: Services, Add to MonoAgent Tasks
emptyBy.ready: Approve tasks from Inbox so agents can pick them up

capture.title: How to capture
capture.chrome: In Chrome: highlight text, then choose MonoAgent, Add selection as task.
capture.mac: On a Mac: select text in any app, then Services, Add to MonoAgent Tasks.
capture.agents: Agents add tasks through the task tools; their work shows here within seconds.

tasks.hasNotes: This card has notes: open it to read them

publication.title: Publication
publication.subtitle: {{count}} publications in this profile
publication.emptyHint: Successful publications appear here automatically. Try changing your filters.

ask.subject: Subject
ask.textLabel: Exact text that will be sent
ask.unreviewable: Can't be reviewed here ({{why}}), so it can't be approved: reject it, or change the step and run it again.
ask.preparedBy: Prepared by {{name}}. Nothing is sent until you approve.
ask.preparedByClaim: Prepared by an agent that says it is {{name}}. Nothing is sent until you approve.

info.title: Info
info.subtitle: Details MonoAgent fills into websites for you. Anything the AI missed, add yourself.
info.subtitleBusiness: Company details MonoAgent fills into websites for you, including who owns and runs the business. Your personal details are kept and come back if you switch to Person.
info.typeFailed: Could not change the profile type: {{message}}
info.aiFillHint: Fills empty fields from your documents. Never changes what you typed.
info.aiDone_one: Filled {{count}} field from your documents, {{empty}} left empty
info.aiDone_other: Filled {{count}} fields from your documents, {{empty}} left empty
info.aiNothing: Nothing new found in your documents, {{empty}} left empty
info.aiFromUnknown: Filled by AI from your documents
info.revealed: Shown until you hide it again, or after a minute
info.cardNote: Stored encrypted on this computer. Never sent to an AI. It is filled into a website only when you press Fill card in the browser extension.

coderDefault.label: Default access for new chats
coderDefault.hint: What a new chat starts at when Coder mode is on and a runtime is ready. You can still pick another level in each chat.
coderDefault.off: Coder mode is off, so new chats start Scoped.
coderDefault.allowsFull: Runs commands and changes files in the folder you pick, without asking.
coderDefault.allowsWorkspace: Runs commands and changes files in the folder you pick, without asking, and knows about your profile.

taskResult.previewError: Could not check the proposed change: {{error}}
taskResult.previewInvalid: The proposed change cannot be applied.
taskResult.applied: Applied {{count}} edits. Review and approve the workflow before it runs.
taskResult.adviceOnly: This is advice only. Nothing can be applied automatically.
taskResult.saved: Saved as a draft: needs your approval before it can run
taskResult.stale: The workflow changed since this was proposed: ask again.
taskResult.operatorOnly: Only you can apply this, from the app window.
taskResult.activeBody: This workflow is active: it is running or scheduled, so the change takes effect for its next run. Apply it anyway?
taskResult.activeDeclined: The workflow is active, so the fix was not applied.
taskResult.changedSincePreview: The workflow changed after you reviewed this: nothing was applied. Review it again.
taskResult.tooLarge: This proposal is bigger than the review can show: ask again for a smaller change.
taskResult.tooBigToReview: This change is bigger than the review can show, so it cannot be applied from here. Ask again for a smaller change.
taskResult.applyBody: This changes {{fields}} in {{nodes}} of the workflow "{{name}}". The workflow will need your approval again before it runs.

coderOrg.title: Coder chat team and sends
coderOrg.machineHint: How a coder chat's lead staffs its workers, and whether what agents send waits for you. For this whole computer.
coderOrg.routerHint: When a coder chat's lead starts a worker without naming its role and skills.
coderOrg.routerJevNote: With a Jev key set, a worker's brief goes to Jev (TypeSafe) whatever you pick here: Automatic and TypeSafe Jev route with it, and Jev picks the model and effort the lead leaves open. Only removing the Jev key keeps briefs on this machine.

routerDesc.auto: monomind's picker when it is confident, else Jev, else the lead.
routerDesc.jev: Jev picks the role and skills.
routerDesc.model: The lead names roles from its org roster.

coderOrg.sendApproval: Agents' sends wait for my approval
coderOrg.sendApprovalHint: Email, direct messages, comments, posts, connection requests and publishing that an agent prepares wait on a card until you approve them. Destinations you always allow go out without asking.
coderOrg.sendApprovalOffBody: Agents could send email, direct messages, comments and posts, and publish, as you, without asking you first. A page or message an agent reads can steer it.
coderOrg.allowHint: An agent's sends to these go out without asking, for this profile. A card's Always allow adds one. To add one here, write the action, platform, account and recipient exactly as the card shows them.
coderOrg.allowRecipientPlaceholder: Profile URL, address or name, as the card shows it
coderOrg.allowRecipientLabel: That reads like a description, not an address: write the profile URL, address, handle or name the send card shows.
coderOrg.alwaysAllowBody: This sends this {{channel}} now, and from now on an agent's {{channel}} to {{recipient}} from {{account}} goes out without asking you.
coderOrg.appAccess: Coder agents are told about MonoAgent
coderOrg.appAccessHint: On: coder prompts carry the profile's summary, and org workers are offered MonoAgent's tabs (tasks, documents, people, vault, workflows and apps) and told how to use them. Off: org workers aren't told about or offered MonoAgent's tabs, and agents get no profile summary; the coder lead keeps full access, operator-only commands and send approval still apply.

toolLinks.vaultHidden: A vault command: its values are not shown here.

history.title: History
history.emptyHint: Start a chat and it shows up here, together with your org runs.
history.warning_one: {{count}} org could not report its runs: {{names}}
history.warning_other: {{count}} orgs could not report their runs: {{names}}
history.confirmDeleteBody_one: Delete {{count}} chat? Its messages are removed for good.
history.confirmDeleteBody_other: Delete {{count}} chats? Their messages are removed for good.
history.clearAllBody_one: Delete {{count}} chat? Org runs are kept.
history.clearAllBody_other: Delete all {{count}} chats? Org runs are kept.
history.clearAllNone: There are no chats to clear.
history.stillActive_one: {{count}} chat was kept: it is still running. Stop its turn first.
history.stillActive_other: {{count}} chats were kept: they are still running. Stop their turns first.
